Medium
Student Mode: quiz practice only — answer pages and teacher tools are hidden.
Presets:
Protocol & replay tools (advanced)
Machine-readable capabilities, optional diagnostic provenance, archival replay, and local curriculum profiles. Diagnostics are off by default.
Saved blueprints:
Personal practice history (local files)
Import your own EquationWright result JSON files to see accuracy and completion over time. History stays in this tab; it is not uploaded or automatically saved.
Class tools (collect & analyze results)
Privacy: students submit under an alias they choose (e.g. Student-17) — never collect real names. The collector belongs to you (Google Apps Script, Formspree, etc.), not to this app. Beta note: anyone with the submit URL can post to it — this is homework collection, not secure testing.
AI tutor (bring your own key)
Calls go directly from your browser to the provider — this app has no server and never sees your key. The AI never does math: it reads your labeled mistakes and prescribes a drill; the app generates and grades it.
Analysis sends your quiz results to your chosen AI provider — aliases only, never real names. A typical diagnosis costs well under a cent on a small model (Haiku, Gemini Flash).
Offline math engine (optional)
By default, math rendering loads MathJax from a CDN (needs internet once; then your browser caches it). To go truly offline: download https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-svg.js (one ~2 MB file, no fonts needed), save it as mathjax/tex-svg.js in a folder next to this HTML file, and it will be found automatically when you open the app from your disk. Or point at any custom copy below.
